cyclone.title: Cyclone Preparedness & Response
dos: Inspect your house; secure loose roof tiles, tin sheets, and overhangs.
Store at least 72 hours of drinking water in clean covered containers.
Keep battery-powered torches, portable power banks, and non-perishable dry rations ready.
Keep livestock untied if safe shelter cannot accommodate them, allowing them to flee rising water.
Turn off central gas valves and main electrical circuit breakers if flooding starts.
donts: Do NOT venture outside when the eye of the storm passes (winds temporarily drop, but fierce reverse gusts follow immediately).
Do NOT touch downed power lines or step into puddles near broken utility poles.
Do NOT rely on unverified social media voice notes — monitor official All India Radio / DD Sahyadri/Odia broadcasts.
Do NOT drive through flooded bridges or causeways (less than 30 cm of moving water can float a vehicle).
whenToSeekHelp: Structural roof collapse or wall breach.
Severe penetrating traumatic injury or profuse bleeding.
Rising flood waters exceeding knee height with no upper floor access.

flood.title: Flooding & Waterlogging Response
dos: Move immediately to the highest accessible floor or designated cyclone/flood shelter.
Boil all drinking water for at least 3 minutes, or use chlorine purification tablets (1 tablet per 20L).
Keep identification documents, land titles, and medicines in double-sealed waterproof plastic zip pouches.
Signal rescue teams using bright cloth, whistles (3 short blasts is universal emergency signal), or torch flashes.
donts: Do NOT walk barefoot through stagnant flood water due to high risk of leptospirosis and submerged sharp debris.
Do NOT consume food that has been in contact with flood waters.
Do NOT drink untreated tap or tube-well water in inundated zones.
whenToSeekHelp: Signs of waterborne infection: high fever, muscle cramps, severe vomiting, or dehydration.
Snakebite or deep lacerations from submerged iron rods.
Stranded infants, elderly, or pregnant individuals unable to evacuate.

heatwave.title: Severe Heatwave & Sunstroke
heatwave.source: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / NDMA
dos: Drink oral rehydration salts (ORS), lemon water (nimbu pani), coconut water, or buttermilk frequently.
Wear loose, light-colored, full-sleeve cotton clothing and wide-brim hats or umbrellas.
Move anyone showing dizziness or disorientation into shaded, well-ventilated rooms immediately.
Apply wet cloth packs to the neck, armpits, and groin to rapidly lower core body temperature.
donts: Do NOT leave children or pets inside parked vehicles even for minutes.
Do NOT consume excessive caffeinated drinks or alcohol which exacerbate dehydration.
Do NOT force heavy solid meals on an overheated, nauseous individual.
whenToSeekHelp: Body temperature exceeding 103°F (39.4°C) with dry, hot, red skin (lack of sweating).
Confusion, slurred speech, hallucinations, or loss of consciousness.

traumaFirstAid.title: Traumatic Injury & Bleeding Control
traumaFirstAid.source: Indian Red Cross Society / NDMA First Responder Manual
dos: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure onto bleeding wounds with a clean cloth or bandage for at least 10 minutes without lifting.
Elevate the injured bleeding limb above heart level if no fracture is suspected.
Keep an injured person lying flat and warm to prevent shock.
Immobilize broken limbs using cardboard, wooden splints, or rolled newspapers wrapped snugly with cloth.
donts: Do NOT remove embedded objects (knife, iron rod, glass) from wounds — stabilize the object in place with padding.
Do NOT administer medicines, pain relievers, or sedatives without professional medical advice.
Do NOT give fluids or food to an unconscious or heavily bleeding person.
whenToSeekHelp: Pulsatile, spurting blood that does not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure.
Suspected head, neck, or spine trauma with numbness or loss of sensation.
Open compound fractures where bone is visible.
